transcript: The other night I attended The White Chip, an autobiographical play by Sean Daniels about addiction and recovery. It was quite good. It was quick, 90 minutes, and it was very emotionally effective. Funny, sad, a lot of different things. I also noticed it was very economically staged. The play centers around a man named Steven, played by Joe Tapper, and the two other actors, Crystal Dickinson and Jason Tam, basically come in and out of scenes playing dozens of different people Steven encounters throughout his battle with alcoholism. I was really impressed with the range that all three actors got to showcase throughout this piece, and I was impressed by the story, but I didn't love the direct narration that transitioned us between scenes. That's really just a matter of personal taste, though. One other thing were these almost cartoon like sound effects that underscored the play most frequently in the first half. I just found them not really in line with the tone of the piece in general and just kind of distracting. But this was a pretty minor detail on this game of things. The White Chip is running into early March at MCC's venue and house kitchen with that other playable for my collection.
